name: VA-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's 22-point Republican partisan lean anchors the race firmly on the GOP side
Incumbent Griffith holds a roughly 8-to-1 fundraising edge over challenger Powers
Prediction markets price a Griffith win near 97 percent
No public polls or expert ratings; the Democratic-tilted national environment trims the margin only modestly
model.rationale: The district's 22-point Republican lean, Griffith's incumbency and dominant fundraising advantage, and market pricing near 97 percent for the GOP all point the same direction; the favorable national environment for Democrats shaves a few points off the expected margin but leaves the seat well out of reach.
model.watch: A major scandal, a late surge of outside spending against Griffith, or an unexpectedly strong Democratic wave would be needed to move the race, and none is currently evident.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwest Virginia's 9th District leans heavily Republican, with a partisan lean of roughly 22 points toward the GOP. Morgan Griffith, the Republican incumbent, is on the ballot again after securing renomination, and he holds a commanding financial position: about $2.2 million raised and $879,000 on hand, compared with roughly $257,000 raised and $60,000 on hand for Democrat Joy Powers. No outside spending has been reported on either side.

Prediction markets give Griffith roughly a 97 percent chance of winning, and no public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race. The current national environment leans Democratic, which would trim a few points off the Republican margin in a neutral year, but not nearly enough to put the district in play. All available evidence points to a comfortable Griffith re-election.
